title: More gas in the same vessel
hook: Change amount of gas and predict ideal-gas pressure.
misconception: ideal-gas pressure stays fixed when amount of gas doubles.
objective: Apply P = nRT/V to compare ideal-gas pressure when amount of gas changes, under the stated assumptions.

claims.text: With an ideal gas at fixed volume and absolute temperature, P = nRT/V. When amount of gas doubles, ideal-gas pressure becomes 2 times its original value.
claims.source: Idealized model P = nRT/V; scaling exponent 1. Physics and assumptions await independent review.

recall.question: Consider an ideal gas at fixed volume and absolute temperature, with a nonzero initial result. If amount of gas triples from a positive value, what is the multiplier on ideal-gas pressure?
recall.why: Apply P = nRT/V under the same assumptions: the multiplier is 3.
